discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that time-reversal-invariant band insulators with spin-orbit coupling carry a hidden Z2 topological invariant, predicting the quantum spin Hall state with helical edge channels protected against backscattering. Molenkamp and co-workers realized this state in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, observing quantized edge conduction, the first experimental topological insulator. This work established that the Berry-phase geometry of Bloch electrons, not only symmetry breaking, classifies phases of matter. It launched a vast field: three-dimensional topological insulators, topological superconductors and Majorana modes, Weyl and Dirac semimetals, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and topological classification of materials across thousands of compounds. The concept unifies transport, spectroscopy and materials design, and underpins proposals for dissipationless electronics and topological quantum computation. It is one of the most influential conceptual advances in condensed matter physics of the past two decades.
